title: Victorian event cards and timeline strip
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Victorian Britain and the Industrial Revolution (Revolution)
source: Seeded from history/y6 lesson 14 (Victorian event cards and timeline strip (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 14: Queen Victoria's reign: the Victorian era on a timeline. To understand when the Victorian era was and how it fits into British history

cards:
era
a long period of history with
its own features

reign
the time a king or queen rules

Victorian
from the time of Queen
Victoria, 1837 to 1901

chronology
putting events in time order
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: How old was Victoria when she became queen?
questions.model: She was born in 1819. She became queen in 1837. 1837 minus 1819 = 18.

questions.q: Which came first: the Great Exhibition or the Education Act?
Which era came after the Victorian era?
Make a Victorian timeline from 1837 to 1901 with eight events from the card set, evenly spaced by decade.
questions.a: Events correctly placed by date on a scaled timeline
questions.model: Teacher marks the decades and places 1837 first.

questions.q: Work out how many years after Victoria's crowning each event happened (choose three).
questions.a: For example: Great Exhibition 1851 is 14 years after 1837

questions.q: Is it fair to name an era after a monarch? What else could we call it?
questions.a: For example: the age of steam or railways, because ordinary people drove the change

questions.q: Big question: why is it named after one queen?
questions.a: Her long reign, 1837 to 1901, covered a whole period of great change
